text:
maria: Hey team — customer ACME reported a billing spike. Invoice shows ~3.2M tokens but Console served_tokens for their tenant is ~2.1M for the same period. Any idea why billed > served by ~1.1M? Seen around 2026-03-05 14:00 UTC.

shreya: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the customer_id and a sample request_id (or a few request ids) so we can trace?

maria: customer_id: acme-42
maria: sample req: req_0a1b2c (one example from the spike window)
maria: snippet: `{"model":"rwd-3b-q","input":"Customer: Hi, can you...","headers":{"X-Client-Id":"acme-42"}}`

tom: pulled billing events for acme-42 around that window. Summary: metered_tokens=3201456, served_tokens=2103120. I see a lot of `batch_prefetch=true` events and internal_batch_id blk-9001..blk-9015. Logs (sanitized):
```
{ "ts": "2026-03-05T14:02:10Z", "req_id": "req_0a1b2c", "metered_tokens": 1200, "served_tokens": 800, "prefetch": true, "kv_cache_hit": true }
{ "ts": "2026-03-05T14:02:11Z", "req_id": "req_0b2c3d", "metered_tokens": 1200, "served_tokens": 0, "prefetch": true, "kv_cache_hit": false }
```
(there are hundreds of similar lines)

kevin: quick explanation: this looks like continuous batching + KV-prefetch behaviour. Our runtime will occasionally run speculative/prefetch decode work to warm KV entries or compute shared prefixes for an upcoming batch. Those internal decode operations currently emit meter events at the ingress stage (we count tokens when the decode job is scheduled). If later a KV cache hit or post-batch dedupe means the client does not actually receive those tokens, served_tokens will be lower than metered_tokens.

kevin: TL;DR: metering counts some internal prefetch/generation work. That's intentional historically (we meter work the cluster does), but it creates confusion when customers compare "served" vs invoice. We should make it clearer and give a way to opt into billing only for emitted tokens.

shreya: OK — can you repro locally so support can show ACME? If we can reproduce we can ask billing to refund the extra for this cycle.

kevin: repro steps I used (short):
1) Start a Dedicated pool or local runtime with config: `continuous_batching=true`, `kv_prefetch=true`, `batch_window_ms=20`
2) Send 200 near-identical requests that share a long prefix (e.g., `"Customer: Hello, I need help with order 123"`) with small jitter
3) Collect meter events and final response token counts. You'll see meter_events totals > sum of tokens in responses due to prefetch work.

Command example: 
```
curl -X POST https://internal-runtime/repro/run -H "X-Internal-Id: repro-185112" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b-q","continuous_batching":true,"kv_prefetch":true,"inputs":["Customer: Hello,..." x200]}'
```
(I used a script that sends parallel requests with identical prefixes)

tom: thanks. From billing side: history — we meter at the `ingress.meter_event` which is emitted before final dedupe/cache logic. Quick mitigation: we can filter meter events that have `event_type: "prefetch_internal"` or `prefetch=true` and not count them for invoices. I'll open a billing patch, but we need to coordinate with runtime so we don't double-count other cases.

kevin: implementation note: we already tag prefetch jobs with `meter_tag=prefetch_internal` and include `prefetch_trace_id`. We can update the billing pipeline (beam job) to drop meter events with that tag for tenant-billed aggregates. Patch in staging now.

shreya: customer asks about workaround now — what can they do to avoid future surprises?

kevin: two options:
- short-term workaround: set tenant config `kv_prefetch=false` or `continuous_batching=false` for their Dedicated pool if they need strictly served-token billing parity. This may increase latency/cost slightly.
- medium-term: we'll add a tenant-level flag `billing_meter_mode = "served_tokens" | "work_done"` (default remains work_done). We can flip acme-42 to `served_tokens` for next cycle once the pipeline patch is validated.

maria: can billing confirm credit for the ~1.1M token difference while you patch? ACME is unhappy.

shreya: yes — I've created an internal billing ticket #BILL-3221, flagged for urgent review and credit estimate. We won't auto-credit until engineering verifies the filter doesn't hide legitimate work.

ops-bot: deploy-status: billing/filter-prefetch PATCH to staging succeeded (deploy_id: deploy-2026-03-08-901).

tom: after running the staging filter over the spike window (recompute aggregate with prefetch events removed), billed_tokens drops by ~1.05M for acme-42. We're prepping a safe prod rollout and will update the invoice or issue a one-time credit depending on finance.

kevin: followups: I'll add a small doc in product (and a Console tooltip) explaining the difference: "metered tokens: includes internal prefetch/batching work; served tokens: tokens returned to your app." Also adding an opt-in billing_mode as mentioned.

maria: thanks — pls keep me posted. ACME prefers credit rather than toggling runtime flags.

shreya: we will coordinate with finance and ops. I'll update ticket #BILL-3221 and DM the account owner.

maria: appreciate the quick turnaround :pray:
